views.title: The homogeneous equation
notes: Try an exponential and solve its characteristic equation

views.title: Underdamped motion
equations: x_h(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\left(C_1\cos w t+C_2\sin w t\right)
notes: The envelope decays while the phase rotates
A circle in phase space becomes an inward spiral

views.title: Complex forcing
notes: Differentiate by multiplication in the complex plane
The physical displacement is the real projection

views.title: The transfer function
notes: Multiply by the complex conjugate
The denominator controls both amplitude and phase

views.title: Amplitude and phase
notes: Choose the phase quadrant from the complex denominator
At the natural frequency the response lags by a quarter turn

views.title: Dimensionless resonance
notes: Frequency ratio and damping ratio collapse the parameters
Maximizing amplitude means minimizing the denominator

views.title: Locate the peak
notes: The nonzero stationary point gives the resonance peak
Damping shifts the peak below the natural frequency

views.title: Peak height
notes: Substitute the peak frequency into the denominator
A narrow high peak accompanies weak damping

views.title: Restore initial conditions
notes: The transient makes the initial position and velocity fit
Long after the start, only the periodic response remains

views.title: Energy balance
notes: The drive replenishes the energy removed by damping
Steady periodic motion has zero average stored-energy change

views.title: One equation, connected views
equations: x(t)=e^{-\gamma t}(C_1\cos w t+C_2\sin w t)+|X|\cos(\omega t-\phi)
notes: Exponential decay describes the transient
Complex vectors explain amplitude and phase
The resonance curve predicts the strongest response
